LESSON: PARTS OF A PLANT • LEAVES • FLOWER • STEM

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Our Neighbourhood
Topic 4.3: Parts of a plant • Leaves • Flower • Stem
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Parts of a plant • Leaves • Flower • Stem, part of Our Neighbourhood in SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have plants? 2. Why are different parts of a plant important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Parts of a plant • Leaves • Flower • Stem together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner develops concepts of parts of a plant when exploring and manipulating parts of a plant.

Values:
Responsibility: as learner and cares for plants within the immediate environment by watering them.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Environmental education: learner enhances environmental awareness when taking a nature walk round the school garden.

Link to other learning area:

Concepts of plants such as parts of plants (leaf) relates to concepts of leaf printing in Creative Activities

Suggested Learning Resources

Charts on parts of a plant, picture cards, flash cards, braille cards, glue, crayons, realia, coloured pencil, photos, paint, cardboard, manila papers,

young uprooted plants, school environment and digital devices with assistive technology
